question: If the current passing through a heater is tripled by keeping resistance and time of the current flow unaltered, then the heat produced is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Becomes nine times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The heat produced in a resistor is given by the formula **H = I²RT**.
 
• If the current (I) is tripled, then the new current is 3I.
 
• Substituting the new current into the formula, the heat produced becomes **(3I)²RT = 9I²RT**.
 
• This shows that the heat produced is **nine times** the original heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current (I)**

 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge in a conductor.
 
• It is measured in amperes (A).
 
• Current can be direct (DC) or alternating (AC).
 
 
 
• **Resistance (R)**
 
 
• Resistance is the opposition to the flow of electric current.
 
• It is measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• Materials with high resistance are called insulators, while those with low resistance are called conductors.
 
 
 
• **Heat (H)**
 
 
• Heat produced in a resistor due to current flow is known as Joule heating.
 
• It is given by the formula H = I²RT, where I is current, R is resistance, and T is time.
 
• Joule heating is used in applications like electric heaters and incandescent bulbs.
 
 
 
• **Time (T)**
 
 
• Time is the duration for which the current flows through the resistor.
 
• It is usually measured in seconds (s).
